checked.text: an exclave of Russia between Lithuania and Poland
bordered by Poland to the south, Lithuania to the north and east, and the Baltic Sea to the west
until 1946 known in English as Königsberg
was a German city established in the 13th century
Founded in 1255 on the site of the Old Prussian settlement Twangste by the Teutonic Knights
By the act of coronation in Königsberg Castle on 18 January 1701
became Frederick I, King in Prussia
who lived there virtually all his life
In 1944, Königsberg suffered heavy damage from British bombing attacks and burned for several days
captured by the Soviet Union on 9 April 1945
agreed in principle to the proposal of the Soviet Government concerning the ultimate transfer to the Soviet Union of the City of Koenigsberg
renamed Kaliningrad in July 1946 in honour of Mikhail Kalinin
Kalinin was unrelated to the city
All military and civilian land links between the region and the rest of Russia now must pass through members of NATO and the EU
after the defeat of Nazi Germany became part of the Soviet Union and was renamed to Kaliningrad in 1946
After the fall of the USSR, Kaliningrad became part of Russia
